title: TIME JUMP: 07:00 Tuesday, Quinlan Speeds Up and H Moves to 12:00 Wednesday

fields.jumpLabel: Clock advances to 07:00 CDT, one hour after STARTEX
fields.scenarioTitle: Clearance Time — Evacuation Decision & Vertical Critical-Care Moves
fields.narration:
EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 07:00 CDT, Tuesday, September 15, 2026. Over the last hour the Zone A evacuation has picked up. Contraflow is still running outbound on US 181. The 14 Gulf Nurse Staffing nurses are still stuck in Portland. The census has not changed: 12 NICU infants, 3 of them on ventilators, and 19 ICU patients, 6 of them on ventilators. Outer rain bands are crossing the bay, with gusts to 30 miles per hour.

Two new products have just arrived in the command center.

First product: "EXERCISE. BULLETIN. HURRICANE QUINLAN SPECIAL ADVISORY NUMBER 15. NWS NATIONAL HURRICANE CENTER MIAMI FL AL172026. 700 AM CDT TUE SEP 15 2026. ...QUINLAN FORECAST TO MOVE FASTER TOWARD THE MIDDLE TEXAS COAST... LOCATION 25.2N 93.0W, ABOUT 300 MI SE OF CORPUS CHRISTI. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS 120 MPH. MOVEMENT NW AT 8 MPH. A FASTER NORTHWEST MOTION IS EXPECTED TONIGHT. TROPICAL-STORM-FORCE WINDS EXTEND OUTWARD UP TO 60 MILES. Tropical-storm-force winds are now expected on the coast near Corpus Christi around 12:00 CDT Wednesday, about 6 hours earlier than the previous forecast. Landfall is expected Wednesday afternoon. Corpus Christi wind speed probabilities: 34 knots 94 percent, 50 knots 72 percent, 64 knots 51 percent. The STORM SURGE WARNING remains in effect from Baffin Bay to Port O'Connor, including Corpus Christi Bay: 4 to 6 feet. End of product. EXERCISE."

Second product: "WTUS84 KCRP 151215. HLSCRP. EXERCISE EXERCISE. Hurricane Quinlan Local Statement Advisory Number 15. NWS Corpus Christi TX. 715 AM CDT Tue Sep 15 2026. ...STORM SURGE WARNING AND HURRICANE WARNING IN EFFECT FOR COASTAL NUECES... Tropical storm conditions arrive late Wednesday morning. Complete preparations by tonight. Low-lying roads, including the approaches to the causeways and the low points on I-37, may flood before the strongest winds arrive. End of product. EXERCISE."

The arrival of tropical-storm-force winds, which this hospital's plan calls H, has moved from 18:00 Wednesday to 12:00 Wednesday. Every clock that counts down to H is now 6 hours shorter.
worldState: Time is 07:00 CDT, Tuesday, September 15, 2026. Weather: outer bands crossing Corpus Christi Bay, gusts to 30 mph.
NHC Special Advisory 15 (07:00 CDT): Quinlan is 120 mph and moving NW at 8 mph, 300 miles SE of Corpus Christi, and is expected to speed up tonight. The 34-knot probability for Corpus Christi is 94%.
H (tropical-storm-force winds at Corpus Christi) is now 12:00 CDT Wednesday, September 16, not 18:00.
Under the 12-hour clearance rule, the final horizontal evacuation order deadline is now 00:00 tonight, 17 hours from now. It is no longer 06:00 Wednesday.
Vertical Evacuation Phase 1 (NICU to 7 West, ICU to 6 West) is now due by 06:00 Wednesday.

The Storm Surge Warning (4 to 6 ft) and the Hurricane Warning remain in effect for coastal Nueces County. NWS Corpus Christi says low roads, causeway approaches and the I-37 low points may flood before the strongest winds.

San Antonio round trips are still about 5.5 hours. Any ambulance transfer planned for Wednesday morning would now be on the road in tropical-storm-force wind. Coastal AirCare 2 is grounded once winds reach a sustained 34 kt or when the pilot decides.
Zone A evacuation is under way and US 181 contraflow is outbound only. Zone B still has no evacuation order.
The 14 Gulf Nurse Staffing RNs are still in Portland and cannot cross.
Census unchanged: 12 NICU infants (3 ventilated) on floor 2 and 19 ICU patients (6 ventilated) on floor 3.
fields.facilitatorNote: Watch for the IC to formally reset the timeline to H = 12:00 Wednesday and announce the new deadlines (horizontal decision by 00:00, Vertical Evacuation Phase 1 by 06:00). Also watch for the TCL to drop or move up transfers that can no longer finish before H. Prompt the CNO if needed: the plan's H−24 staffing check now falls at 12:00 today, and the agency gap means less than 90% of ride-out nurses.

instructorNote: This card moves H 6 hours earlier and tests whether command rebuilds the timeline instead of working to the old 06:00 Wednesday deadline. The IC should announce the new deadlines, the TCL should re-plan transfers that cannot finish before 12:00 Wednesday, and the CNO should re-check ride-out ratios against the shorter clock.
